prompt: A channel's sales fell while its average ticket stayed the same. Where does that point first?
hint: Sales = orders × average ticket.

choices.text: At prices and discounts
choices.why: Those would move the average ticket, and the ticket did not move.

choices.text: At fewer orders: traffic, a campaign or stock
choices.why: Right: with the ticket unchanged, the whole fall is in the count of orders.

choices.text: At the mix of products sold, with cheaper items replacing dearer ones
choices.why: A cheaper mix lowers the average ticket, which stayed put.

choices.text: Nowhere yet: the ticket says nothing
choices.why: An unchanged ticket rules out a whole list of causes, which is why the split is made first.

prompt: An online shop took 2,400 orders in a month at an average ticket of R$ 450. What were its sales, in thousands of reais?
hint: Orders times ticket, divided by 1,000.

prompt: Lívia split October by channel and found every store growing. Why did she not split the stores by category as well?
hint: When does a tree stop?

choices.text: Varanda's data has no categories for the stores
choices.why: It has: each store is its five categories added up.

choices.text: A tree should never go below two levels
choices.why: The online branch went to a third level. The depth follows the change, not a rule.

choices.text: The change sat in the online branch, so the stores held nothing to explain
choices.why: Right: stop splitting when one branch holds the change and its siblings do not.

choices.text: Splitting by category would change the total being explained
choices.why: A correct split adds back to its parent, so the total stays the same; it would just be wasted work here.

prompt: A channel's sales are its number of orders multiplied by its average ___.
hint: R$ 350 at the online shop, both Octobers.

prompt: At the Pampulha store, receipts in March were the same as a year before, and sales fell 8%. Which list of suspects should Lívia test first?
hint: Which factor of the tree moved?

choices.text: Traffic and the weather, since fewer people came in
choices.why: The receipts were the same, so the same number of people bought.

choices.text: A broken pipeline that lost receipts
choices.why: Lost receipts would lower the count of receipts, and the count held.

choices.text: The calendar, comparing the number of weekend days in both Marches
choices.why: Fewer weekend days would mean fewer visits and receipts; the receipts did not move.

choices.text: Prices, discounts and the mix of products
choices.why: Right: with receipts flat, the 8% is in the average ticket, and those are the ticket's causes.

prompt: In your sheet, how many percentage points did the online shop contribute to October's change? Give the sign.
Why does Lívia read each line's contribution in points rather than each line's own growth rate?
hint: Nova Lima and a store a tenth its size.

choices.text: Points weigh each line by its size; growth rates ignore size
choices.why: Right: a small line growing fast and a large line growing slowly can move the company by the same amount.

choices.text: Growth rates cannot be computed for the online shop, which is not a store
choices.why: The sheet computes it: −21.2%.

choices.text: Points are rounded less, so the column adds to exactly −0.7
choices.why: They are rounded too, and the rounded column adds to −0.8.

choices.text: Growth rates are for years, and points are for months
choices.why: Both work for any period; they answer different questions.

prompt: What is the first check the lesson asks of any breakdown, before reading it?

choices.text: That every line has grown, or that every line has fallen, in the same direction as the total
choices.why: Lines move in different directions all the time; in October nine grew and one fell.

choices.text: That the parts add back to the total being explained
choices.why: Right: otherwise some sales are in the total and in no line, and the diagnosis is about the wrong number.

choices.text: That the largest line is first
choices.why: Order on the page changes nothing about where the change sits.

choices.text: That the percentages are rounded to one decimal place
choices.why: Rounding is presentation. A breakdown that does not add up is wrong at any rounding.

prompt: A company sold 1,200 last year. One of its lines went from 150 to 180. How many percentage points did that line add to the company's growth, to one decimal?
hint: The line's change divided by the whole of last year.

prompt: Which of these were on Lívia's list of suspects for October? Choose all that apply.
hint: Five rows, and the data was one of them.

choices.text: The calendar: weekend days and holidays
choices.why: Right: 8 weekend days in both Octobers, and the holiday on a weekend in both.

choices.text: The data itself: whether the pipeline lost orders
choices.why: Right: the cheapest suspect to test, and it produces the same shape.

choices.text: The number of people working in each store
choices.why: The stores grew; the fall was online, so staff in the stores could not explain it.

choices.text: Campaigns run in one October and not the other
choices.why: Right: the one suspect left standing.

prompt: Why does the lesson put "the data itself" on the list of suspects?
hint: What would three missing days of orders look like?

choices.text: Because Tiago Ramos had broken the pipeline before
choices.why: The lesson blames nobody. The data is a suspect in every diagnosis, whoever runs it.

choices.text: A pipeline that stops copying orders produces the same shape, and it is cheap to test
choices.why: Right: one channel falling at an unchanged ticket is exactly what lost orders look like.

choices.text: Because a diagnosis should start by doubting every number in the report
choices.why: Doubting everything tests nothing. The data is on the list because it fits this shape.

choices.text: Because online data is less reliable than store data
choices.why: Neither channel is assumed worse; the count was simply checked, and it matched.

prompt: Lívia split October 2024 at the campaign and compared it with October 2025. Which result would have counted against the campaign as the cause?
hint: What should ordinary days look like if only the campaign moved?

choices.text: October 2024's campaign days averaging more orders than its ordinary days
choices.why: That is what a campaign does, and it is what the test found: 195.8 against 88.

choices.text: November 2025's online sales growing faster than November 2024's
choices.why: That supports the move: what October lost, November gained.

choices.text: October 2025's ordinary days averaging fewer orders than October 2024's ordinary days
choices.why: Right: then customers would have been lost on ordinary days too, and the campaign could not be the whole story. They averaged 99.5 against 88.

choices.text: The average ticket being R$ 350 in both Octobers
choices.why: An unchanged ticket is what losing a campaign's orders looks like, so it fits the campaign.

prompt: Put the steps of Lívia's diagnosis of October in order.
hint: From where the change sits to how it is worded.
items: Break the total down until one branch holds the change
Write down every suspect for that branch
Test each suspect against the data
Write the finding: what was found, checked and left open
trap: Listing suspects before breaking the number down is the tempting order, and it sends you testing the weather against a fall that sits in one channel.

prompt: Varanda's online ad spend and its sales are both highest in November and December. Why can the data not say the ads caused the sales?
hint: Why does Varanda spend more in those months?

choices.text: Because there are only two months of data
choices.why: There are twelve months every year; more months of the same pattern would not separate the two.

choices.text: Because advertising has no effect on sales
choices.why: The lesson does not say that. It says this comparison cannot measure the effect.

choices.text: The season drives both
choices.why: Right: Varanda spends more because those are the buying months, so the season is a confounder.

choices.text: Because the spend is recorded in a different system from the sales
choices.why: Where the data lives says nothing about cause; joining the two would still leave the season in both.

prompt: Which sentence reports Lívia's finding on October the way the lesson recommends?
hint: Found, consistent with, checked, open.

choices.text: October fell because the campaign moved to November, as the data proves.
choices.why: "Proves" claims an experiment nobody ran, and the sentence hides what is still open.

choices.text: The fall is in online orders and matches the campaign days; calendar, prices, stock and data were checked; a gap is left open.
choices.why: Right: what was found, what it is consistent with, what was ruled out and what is still open.

choices.text: October probably fell for several reasons, and more data is needed.
choices.why: It hedges without saying anything that was found or checked.

choices.text: October fell 0.7%.
choices.why: True, and descriptive. A diagnosis has to add where the change sits and what explains it.

prompt: Match each kind of evidence to what Lívia found for the campaign.
hint: Timing, place, mechanism, the others.

pairs.right: The missing orders match the eleven campaign days and reappear in November
The fall is in the online shop and in no store
Fewer orders at an unchanged ticket
Calendar, prices, stock and the pipeline did not change

prompt: A third thing that moves both of the things being compared, such as the season behind ad spend and sales, is called a ___.
hint: It confounds the comparison.

prompt: Betim's sales rose 10% in the month a new manager arrived. Helena wants to credit the manager. What should Lívia check first?
hint: What else changed for every store that month?

choices.text: How the other stores did that month
choices.why: Right: if every store rose about 10%, something they share explains it, and the manager is not the cause.

choices.text: Whether the manager has a good record from a previous job
choices.why: A good record makes the story attractive; it does not test it against what else changed.

choices.text: Whether Betim's growth is statistically significant, before anything else
choices.why: Significance would not separate the manager from a month every store shared.

choices.text: Nothing: the timing fits, so the manager caused it
choices.why: Timing is one kind of evidence of four, and the cheapest to fake by coincidence.

prompt: A store sold 1,300 thousand reais in a month last year and 1,250 thousand in the same month this year. What is its growth, in percent to one decimal, with its sign?
hint: New over old, minus one.

prompt: In another month, the online shop's sales fell 15%, its orders were flat, and its average ticket fell 15%. Which suspect from Lívia's list deserves the first test?
hint: Which factor moved this time?

choices.text: Campaigns, because a moved campaign explained October
choices.why: A moved campaign showed up as fewer orders. Here the orders held.

choices.text: Prices
choices.why: Right: the whole fall is in the ticket, and a discount or a price cut moves the ticket.

choices.text: The calendar, since a month with fewer weekends has fewer buyers
choices.why: Fewer buyers would mean fewer orders, and the orders were flat.

choices.text: The pipeline, which loses orders when it stops
choices.why: Lost orders lower the count of orders; the count did not move.

prompt: Which of these make a cause more believable when no experiment was run? Choose all that apply.
hint: Four kinds of evidence, and one of these is not evidence.

choices.text: The change sits in the part of the business the cause acts on, and nowhere else
choices.why: Right: the place fits.

choices.text: The other suspects were tested and ruled out
choices.why: Right: a cause left standing after a real list was tested is worth more than the first one liked.

choices.text: Two things rose and fell together over the year
choices.why: That is a correlation, and a confounder such as the season produces one without any cause between them.

choices.text: Everybody at the Monday meeting agrees with it
choices.why: Agreement is how the first explanation somebody likes stops being checked.

choices.text: The mechanism fits: the change looks the way this cause would make it look
choices.why: Right: fewer orders at an unchanged ticket is what losing a campaign looks like.
